rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm guarded against: a reader stuck on a pronoun/noun with no antecedent. Chunk0 line 7 'the audit' and 'the scoped task' resolve via the module-arc-beats carve-out — confirmed this session: `grep -n "audit" curriculum/exercises/walk-and-send-off.md` returns line 44 'Ask Claude to run the audit as a subagent and return a ranked top-five.', and `run-the-first-experiment.md:39-41` places that exercise immediately before this one in module include order, so 'the audit' is the beat the student's own session just ran. Chunk1 line 21 'this one'/'that file' resolve in-chunk (the scrollback file named in the same sentence). Chunk2 line 29 'this commit' resolves against the same chunk's own 'Ask Claude to commit current state...' line — same-slide forward reference, not a pointer to a later slide. Chunk3 line 38 'The commit' continues chunk2's referent (sequential same-file callback, permitted). Chunk4 line 48 'the scoped task' and the expanded prompt's 'the task we scoped earlier in this session' reuse the chunk0 referent plus the session-artifact carve-out. Chunk5 line 56 'The trace' is the closest call: not literally named earlier in this file (Phase 1 uses 'record'/'scrollback'/'transcript path' instead), but 'trace' is arc-earned M4 vocabulary established earlier in this same module's own included files — confirmed this session: `grep -n "\btrace\b" curriculum/lectures/test-and-learn.md` hits line 20 ('A short session with useful observations beats hours of trace you can't read') and `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md` Key Concepts line 50 ('Traces are data.'); both sit earlier in this module's include order (`test-and-learn.md` is the third of three opening lectures, `run-the-first-experiment.md`'s own signposting is chunk-0-equivalent context for every included file), so per §1's carve-out this counts as prior context rather than a never-named term. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Harm guarded against: a callback that only resolves if the reader knows which file sits at a given position in delivery order. Scanned all 6 chunks: no phrasing of the form 'the opening lecture said' or any pointer to another file's content by position. Closest candidate, chunk3 line 38 'the next module forks from the local commit', is a workflow statement about what M5 does with an artefact this file produces, not a quote or claim borrowed from another file's specific passage — it names the relationship functionally, not by locating content inside M5. Not a §2 violation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm guarded against: a 'the X you did' phrase pointing at a beat a rewrite has since cut, stranding the student. Only backward reference in body is chunk0 line 7 'The same session that ran the audit.' Ran this session: `grep -n "audit" curriculum/exercises/walk-and-send-off.md` — line 44 'Ask Claude to run the audit as a subagent and return a ranked top-five.' confirms the beat exists, and `run-the-first-experiment.md` lines 39-41 confirm walk-and-send-off.md sits immediately before this file in the module's current include order. Beat exists, placement current.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: na_reason: no guess/predict-before-reveal construct in file — confirmed this session: `grep -in "guess\|predict\|before you watch\|reveal" curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--set-the-markers-send-it-off.body.txt` returned zero hits. Every chunk is instruction-then-prompt, no predict/observe pairing for this rule to apply to.

Harm guarded against: a slide that says nothing standalone. Ran this session: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md` -> 'files: 1  slides: 5  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets  oversized: 0 / every slide is within limits' (the 5 counted slides are chunks 1-5; chunk0 is the title slide). Read each chunk for standalone content: chunk1 carries a grounding bullet plus an actionable ask plus a prompt; chunk3 (the shortest, optional-push chunk) still carries a self-carrying claim (default is local; here is the optional push) plus its own prompt. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Closest call: chunk1 header 'Phase 1: Set the two return markers' (line 17) only executes ONE of the two markers (the transcript path) inside its own chunk boundary (17-26); the second marker (the starting-point commit) is set two chunks later. Read as a phase-opening umbrella header spanning the following sibling `##` headings under it (mirroring the file's own 'Phase 2: Send it off' pattern, and matching rule 15's explicit allowance for phase-label headers), the content does not CONTRADICT the header — it partially fulfils a claim the phase as a whole completes, which is the stated test ('a header the chunk's own content contradicts fails'), not literal per-chunk completeness. All other headers ('Pin the starting point', 'Push it only if you want it off this laptop', 'Phase 2: Send it off', 'Nudge sparingly while it runs') are fully borne out by their own chunk's content on inspection.

Checked all six sub-items across all six chunks by re-reading the expanded view (`node scripts/expand-md.js`, run this session): no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative (no 'one of the most useful' style claim anywhere in body); no abstraction-noun stack (language throughout is concrete: branch, commit, SHA, transcript path, laptop); no verb triplet with an empty leg. One number+retraction candidate: chunk5 line 55 'Past ten or so interventions, you have become the agent; call it and read what is there.' Covered by the maintainer block's still-present dated note (raw line 70, `check_pedagogy.md §16` calibration-vs-prescription boundary, maintainer call 2026-08-02) — accept-with-note, no edit owed, listed in accept_notes_found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran this session: `sed -n '1,61p' curriculum/exercises/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md | grep -n '\*\*[^*]*\*\*'` -> 5 hits, all in chunk0 at lines 3, 5, 9, 11, 13 ('**Time:**', '**Session**', '**What you do:**', '**What you build:**', '**The point:**'), each a short label of 1-3 words, no bold spanning a whole lead sentence. This is the fixed exercise-header metadata template — confirmed this session: `grep -c '^\*\*Time:\*\* \|^\*\*What you do:\*\*\|^\*\*What you build:\*\*\|^\*\*The point:\*\*' curriculum/exercises/*.md | grep -v ':0' | wc -l` -> 40, i.e. all 40 AE101 exercise files use this identical bolded-label shape. Per §9's own stated principle ('before filing any §9 count violation, check whether another rule or the module template requires the bold you are about to charge for'), a template mandated corpus-wide is not chargeable to this file. Chunks 1-5 carry zero bold in prose (fenced prompt content is exempt regardless).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-read all 5 body `##` headings via `node -e "...content.split('<!-- maintainer -->')[0].match(/^##.*/gm)"` (run this session): 'Phase 1: Set the two return markers' and 'Phase 2: Send it off' are phase labels; 'Pin the starting point', 'Push it only if you want it off this laptop', 'Nudge sparingly while it runs' are imperatives. This is an exercise file, so the required grammar is imperative-or-phase-label (not the lecture claim requirement) — every heading conforms; none is a declarative masquerading as a label or vice versa.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked all 7 body bullets against the three low-value classes (doctrine restatement / self-referential design commentary / aphorism kicker). Chunk1's bullet (line 21) names the transcript-file mechanism grounding the ask — an object, not restated doctrine. Chunk2's two bullets (29-30) are a WIP-scoping warning (a tell) and the task.md mechanism (a reason), each distinct from chunk0's 'What you build' line, not a re-announcement of it. Chunk3's bullet (38) gives the reasoning for the optional push (a priority: default-local, throwaway, forkable). Chunk5's three bullets (54-56): a laptop-awake instruction (a move), the ten-or-so calibration + 'call it and read what is there' (a tell, separately covered under rule 7's accept-note), and the stop-if-off-the-rails policy (a priority distinct from chunk0's 'The point' line). Closest call: chunk5 line 56 'The trace is the result either way' echoes M4's own arc-level 'traces are data' framing (confirmed this session: `grep -n "Traces are data" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md` -> line 50, Key Concepts), but it applies that general principle to authorize stopping THIS SPECIFIC run at THIS SPECIFIC moment — a new actionable permission, not a redundant recitation disconnected from the beat. No aphorism kicker or self-referential design commentary found anywhere in body.
